space.description: 'model' (design space, US survey feet) or a sheet id/name (paper space, inches), e.g. 'SH-004' or 'P-201'

layer.description: layer name; defaults to the current layer

start.description: where the traverse begins: a point [x, y] (x = easting, y = northing), or an entity id to continue from its end (start_at says which end; the entity's direction there is the course a leading deflection turns from)

start_at.description: with a start entity: continue from its end (default) or its start

items.description: one course. Straight: a direction (exactly one of bearing, azimuth, deflection, angle_right) and distance. Curve: radius, turn and one of delta, length or chord; it continues the previous course's direction unless chord_bearing places it (a non-tangent curve). Or the course as text: "N 47°30'15\" E 250", "AZ 75.5 250", "33 L 820", "CURVE R=450 LEFT DELTA=33"

bearing.description: quadrant bearing: N 47°30'15" E, S47-30-15W, N47E

azimuth.description: degrees clockwise from north, 0-360 (a number or DMS text)

deflection.description: the angle turned from the previous course, with its side: '33 L', '18°30'00" RT', or a number with right (clockwise) positive; or its size with turn

turn.description: which way a deflection or a curve turns

angle_right.description: angle measured clockwise from the backsight (the previous course run backwards), as a field traverse records it

distance.description: length of a straight course (feet in model)

radius.description: radius of a curve course -- giving one makes the course a curve

chord_bearing.description: a non-tangent curve's chord bearing (or azimuth)

legs.description: the courses in order, each from where the last one ended

initial_bearing.description: the direction a leading deflection or tangent curve turns from, as a quadrant bearing

close.description: the traverse should close on its start: report the misclosure (distance, bearing, precision 1:N) and, when drawing, add the closing course

polyline.description: draw one polyline instead of separate lines (straight courses only; with close it is a closed polyline)
